items.subject: Owner-mirrored competition rasters are not organizer-authenticated
items.detail: The training-feature stack, labels, existing-fault raster, and sample template are restored from hash-pinned public owner-repository mirrors because the sandbox has no organizer login. SHA-256 pins prove integrity relative to the recorded owner revision, not that the bytes are identical to the organizer download.
items.impact: Every data-backed result and artifact is conditional on the mirrored bytes. Do not claim organizer authenticity or official acceptance.
items.mitigation: Record manifest revision, hashes, byte counts and restore receipt; link to the official data page for manual verification; keep all caches outside Git.

items.status: confirmed on restored owner-mirror bytes; template used only for grid/footprint
items.subject: Sample-submission mirror is not an all-zero prediction inside its footprint
items.detail: On the restored, SHA-256-pinned owner-mirror template, 60,988 finite pixels equal 1 inside the 5,167,373-pixel footprint, matching the label positive count. The official problem page calls its sample a total-fault-absence example; this local template instead contains label-like ones and is not organizer-authenticated.
items.impact: Never copy template pixel values as predictions. Use only its profile and finite-pixel mask to derive grid/footprint; generate all in-footprint predictions explicitly.
items.mitigation: The local writer constructs a separate prediction array and checks every footprint pixel; a fresh format receipt is required for any artifact.

items.status: open; manifest notes exact byte identity
items.subject: labels.tif and existing_faults.tif are byte-identical in the owner manifest
items.detail: The checked-in owner-mirror manifest assigns both paths the same SHA-256 and byte count. This was also observed in predecessor records; organizer naming/semantics are not authenticated here.
items.impact: Do not treat the two mirrored filenames as independent label sources or double-count them.
items.mitigation: Preparation uses labels.tif once and records its hash.

items.status: interpretation inherited; not independently recomputed in GEMSDOE29
items.subject: Ambiguous training band `tc` metadata
items.detail: The owner-mirror stack's embedded description is reported to call `tc` a magnetic tilt/curvature derivative, while the predecessor reports its values correlate at Spearman 0.9999 with the USGS GeoDAWN total-count radiometric raster. The H31 repository groups it with thermal/geochemical features based on that prior internal analysis; this correlation is not a new GEMSDOE29 result.
items.impact: Family D assignment is a working interpretation, not an organizer-verified semantic label. Results using family D inherit this caveat.
items.mitigation: Retain the band name, document the interpretation, do not relabel the source raster, and recheck the correlation only from permitted, verified inputs.

items.subject: Reported leaderboard/submission scores lack organizer receipts
items.detail: The preserved project prompt and prior owner materials contain historical score statements. No organizer receipt, live-page contents, account identity, rank, or score-to-file mapping has been retained or independently verified.
items.impact: These are not verified competition facts, training targets, promotion thresholds, or evidence that any local artifact achieved a particular competition score.
items.mitigation: Keep values clearly labelled as owner/user-reported in the local claim register only; do not publish live rankings or monitor/copy leaderboard content without prior written consent.

items.subject: D2.8 owner-mirrored TIFF has no verified score
items.detail: The predecessor registry marks the dotted H19-5 D2.8 TIFF as unscored and not slot-approved. Any association with an earlier user/owner-reported score claim is not a verified score-to-file relationship. GEMSDOE29 locally checked its TIFF against the restored owner-mirror template; this is not organizer authentication or slot approval.
items.impact: The download is a provenance/reference artifact only and must not be presented as a recommended submission.
items.mitigation: Use the `historical_reference` role, a prominent do-not-submit warning, a unique archival filename and a current local format receipt.

items.subject: Component-hide spatial holdout is only a catalogue-gap proxy
items.detail: The hidden holdout traces are components of the existing catalogue, not the organizer's newly expert-labelled faults. The local protocol excludes visible catalogue pixels from its proxy score, but the official problem page does not fully specify those optional mask semantics.
items.impact: Spatial DTI cannot be called a competition score or assumed to predict public/private leaderboard performance. Four quadrants are the spatial replication units; draws are repeated hides.
items.mitigation: Use same-run paired controls, fresh confirmation, raw-cell hashes and explicit proxy language; never use a weekly slot unless the preregistered holdout gate beats the current same-run best.

items.subject: Earlier reported [0,1] upload rejection
items.detail: Predecessor notes report a portal message about predictions outside [0,1] and infer that NaNs inside the owner-mirror footprint may have caused it. No organizer receipt or input file was independently verified here.
items.impact: The historical cause is a hypothesis, not a confirmed platform rule beyond the official range requirement.
items.mitigation: The local writer/checker require finite in-footprint float32 values in [0,1] and separately validate outside-footprint NaNs; the checker does not claim organizer acceptance.

items.subject: GeoDAWN flight-path ZIPs are listed but not validated
items.detail: USGS ScienceBase lists area1 and area2 flight-path archives, but their binary bytes, schema, CRS, coverage, and licence have not been verified in this workspace.
items.impact: H33 acquisition-line feature work must not proceed based only on a catalog listing.
items.mitigation: Leave H33 blocked until the official files are obtained through permitted means and all prerequisites are independently checked.

items.subject: H31 is a regularized worming-like proxy, not a full Poisson-wavelet inversion
items.detail: The available RTP and isostatic-gravity grids are processed through a fixed Fourier 1/k-like scale-space proxy with taper, padding, thresholds, and nearest-maximum tracking. True magnetic field parameters, vendor filter formula, source distribution, remanence, depth, and fault geometry are not independently known.
items.impact: Persistence is not proof of faulting, depth, geothermal activity, or discovery; artifacts and missed edges are possible.
items.mitigation: Use only preregistered settings, name it a proxy, log diagnostics, and require spatial holdout plus fresh confirmation before considering a candidate.

items.subject: Original branch-point checkout was empty
items.detail: At branch-point commit ad130c8d, this repository contained only a one-line README. The main branch subsequently gained the H29 pipeline, evidence and site through PRs #1 and #2; this is now historical context, not the current repository state.
items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.
items.mitigation: The current branch rebases on the latest main and preserves the H29 code/evidence while adding the new H31 research package and Pages workflow.

items.subject: Feature and template footprints differ
items.detail: training_features.tif (owner mirror, sha 4371c82e...) has 5,165,852 finite cells vs the sample_submission template's 5,167,373: 3,061 template-footprint cells are nodata inside the features, and 1,540 feature cells lie outside the template footprint. Any pipeline that assumes 'finite in features == finite in template' silently mis-scores/NaNs 3,061 scored pixels.
items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.
items.mitigation: This repo: worming computes on the FEATURES mask; submission emission is masked to the TEMPLATE footprint and every in-footprint pixel is written finite (0.0/1.0), so the difference cannot produce NaN-inside-footprint. Upstream (competition data) needs owner confirmation that both rasters are authentic copies.

items.subject: Worming citation corrected
items.detail: The project prompt attributes 'worming' to 'Hornby, Boschetti, and Horowitz's multiscale wavelet edge-detection method (1999)' without a venue; the primary source is GJI 137(1):175-196 (wavelet-domain potential-field analysis). A common mis-citation is 'Hornby et al. 1999, Geophysics 64' (that volume/venue pair is the wrong journal).
items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.
items.mitigation: knowledge/01 + README cite GJI 137(1):175-196 with DOI; Horowitz (2018) recorded as the operational recipe source.

items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.

items.subject: Training band `tc` has inherited semantic ambiguity
items.detail: GEMSDOE25 flagged that band 6 'tc' of the official stack (described as magnetic tilt/total-curvature) actually equals the radiometric total-count channel. Re-verified here on read: values are positive (3.7-70.6 range) consistent with radiometric TC, not a magnetic derivative; our RAW_BANDS renames it 'tc_radiometric'.
items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.
items.mitigation: Kept as a radiometric band; no magnetic-edge claims derive from it. Report to organizers if a data erratum channel exists.

items.subject: Measured line-orientation persistence contradicted the naive artifact heuristic
items.detail: After correcting nearest-valid padding and persistence normalization, the current six-level p95 audit gives mean magnetic persistence by strike E-W 0.540, Other 0.491, N-S 0.447. This remains a descriptive strike summary: it neither proves acquisition-line contamination nor supports a simple E-W suppression rule. The current inputs are pinned owner mirrors, not organizer-authenticated.
items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.
items.mitigation: Do not use a simple E-W kill rule. H29-3 spectral-notch work remains a separate registered idea and requires a measured frequency peak first. See current evidence/worming_receipt.json.

items.subject: Historical emission overlaps few potential-field edges
items.detail: On the current nearest-fill, bounded-persistence raster, 1,204/44,090 (2.731%) owner-mirrored D2.8 pixels overlap the union of level-0 p95 magnetic/gravity edges; 579 (1.313%) overlap a joint edge with P>=0.5. The historical score-to-file association remains owner-reported and unauthenticated.
items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.
items.mitigation: The corrected screen tested A1/A2/B1/B2 and H29-5; all five failed the registered +0.005 screen criterion. Do not infer that the geological mechanism is false; see current evidence/h29_holdout.json and knowledge/02_h29_results_2026-10-03.md.

items.subject: Catalogue-gap proxy may miss far-field structure
items.detail: Carried from siblings and re-reviewed in the holdout construction: catalogue-internal hide-and-recover truth sits entirely on catalogue pixels, while a historical owner-mirrored emission’s modeled credit may lie far from them. Proxy gates are conservative for far-field hypotheses and can under-credit a deep-structure detector.
items.impact: This is a carried-forward finding from the earlier main-branch H29 work; review the cited evidence or action before using affected data or interpretations.
items.mitigation: Disclosed in knowledge/01 §6; no arm is ever promoted on proxy evidence alone — pass = 'eligible for a slot decision by the owner', not 'submit'.

items.status: documented; no effect on failed screen decision
items.subject: H29 extra draws and original gate snapshot disagree
items.detail: The archived original H29 raw holdout contained 16 rows for draws 0-3; the screen draws failed, but draws 2-3 had nevertheless been computed and the original gate builder omitted them. Those extra rows were ineligible confirmations and are archived byte-for-byte under evidence/history/h29_holdout_pre_correction_2026-10-03.json. items.subject: The two registered proxies rank candidate files almost oppositely
items.detail: Model-free scoring (evidence/candidate_scoreboard.json): the historical D2.8 geometry scores 0.09832 on the catalogue-hidden proxy and 0.09528 on the SGMC off-catalogue class; the SGMC-inventory emission scores 0.04461 and 0.56153 on the same two targets (a 2.2x loss on one, a 5.9x gain on the other). The H34 screen shows the same sign flip (+0.0535 off-catalogue, -0.0212 catalogue-hidden).
items.impact: Any recommendation depends on which proxy is believed. The repository's historical gates gate on the catalogue-hidden proxy; peer calibration claims the SGMC-style off-catalogue class correlates better with live scores (rho +0.52, n=15, unchecked here).
items.mitigation: Report both proxies for every candidate; never call either a competition score; the system document (knowledge/13) proposes admitting a slot candidate on the off-catalogue class with a bounded catalogue-hidden loss, and this is flagged for the owner because it changes the admission rule.

items.subject: Historical file named 'd2-8' but its 44,090-pixel geometry matches the sibling's d=2.4 sweep point
items.detail: The owner mirror is named ...dotted-h19-5-d2-8... and reports 0.2600; the sibling's latent model describes its 44,090-pixel geometry as the d=2.4 point of a sweep (0.2553, band 0.2500-0.2613). The bytes are unambiguous (44,090 dots, zero catalogue pixels); the label is not.
items.impact: A future reproduction that searches for 'd2.8' parameter provenance may mis-attribute the score.
items.mitigation: Cite the file by content id e56ea318af89 and pixel count, not by the d2.8 label.

items.subject: One programmatic read of the public DrivenData problem-description page during this session
items.detail: Project policy (knowledge/03) is to avoid programmatic contact with drivendata.org because the Terms prohibit robots/automatic access. During this session the public problem-description page was fetched once through the general web-fetch tool to re-verify the metric text already transcribed in the repository. No leaderboard, data tab, login, or account content was accessed, and no polling or copying occurred.
items.impact: A disclosed deviation from the project's own access policy.
items.mitigation: No further programmatic contact; all subsequent verification used public search results, peer-reported staff quotes, and the in-repository transcription. The owner can re-verify the page manually.

items.subject: The coverage module's self-estimated DTI is ~4x optimistic and always selects the largest budget
items.detail: In the H34 screen the module's dti_hat read 0.51-0.68 while the realised masked DTI was 0.12, and it selected the maximum permitted budget (3x control) in every fold, tripling FP mass. The estimator scores parent mass as if it were truth mass.
items.impact: Any budget rule based on this estimator is uncalibrated and will over-emit.
items.mitigation: Recorded as the primary cause of the H34 negative; the system document requires calibrating the prior scale to an expected truth mass before using the marginal-tau budget rule.

items.subject: Sandbox network reaches only GitHub and PyPI, so free official external data cannot be downloaded here
items.detail: curl from the sandbox fails (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL / HTTP 000) for sciencebase.gov, gdr.openei.org, usgs.gov, osti.gov, pubs.usgs.gov, earthquake.usgs.gov, mrdata.usgs.gov, raw.githubusercontent.com and drivendata.org; api.github.com, codeload.github.com and pypi.org work. Re-probed 2026-10-03 (session 4): TLS completes only to api.github.com and pypi.org; additionally maps.usgs.gov, waterdata.usgs.gov, zenodo.org, huggingface.co, doi.org, api.crossref.org, opentopography.org, ornl.gov and scripts.umd.edu fail with SSLZeroReturnError, and usgs.gov, www.nrel.gov, gx.osti.gov, scijournals.usgs.gov, topoinfo.usgs.gov do not resolve.
items.impact: Siler slip/dilation tendency, Peacock & Bedrosian conductance maps and extra 3DEP tiles cannot be fetched in this environment; hypotheses must be written to run on already-mirrored layers or wait for an unrestricted runner.
items.mitigation: All new hypotheses (H35-H39) are specified to run on hash-pinned in-repository layers; external layers are marked optional with DOI and licence verified.

items.subject: Original six-level persistence normalization exceeded its registered range
items.detail: The old formula divided the 0-based last matched level index by n_levels-2, allowing P=1.25. This changed the A1 cutoff and saturated A2 ranks; old evidence/artifacts are not valid for the registered method.
items.impact: Any screen or artifact derived from P>1.0 must not be treated as the preregistered method or a slot candidate.
items.mitigation: Use last_matched_level_index/(n_levels-1), enforce [0,1] at runtime, store amplitude retention separately, and regression-test the bounds. See evidence/history/pre_correction_downloads/ and current evidence/worming_receipt.json.

items.subject: FFT exterior fill was silently replaced with a global median
items.detail: prep_field computed nearest-valid padding and then np.where replaced every invalid cell with the global valid-cell median. This contradicted the frozen H29 preregistration and changes the continued edge field.
items.impact: The bounded-P screen and WORMRANK generated before this fix are not valid for the registered boundary treatment, even though their gate failed.
items.mitigation: Removed the median overwrite, added a regression distinguishing nearest from median fill, and recomputed worming plus all eight screen rows. The intermediate output and hashes are archived in evidence/history/pre_nearest_fill_2026-10-03/; current values are in evidence/worming_receipt.json and evidence/h29_holdout.json.

items.subject: Confirmation model fitting must not precede a passing screen
items.detail: The earlier runner computed draws 2-3 in the same pass as screen draws, so failed arms incurred confirmation fits and the gate could not enforce the staged preregistered rule.
items.impact: Wasted computation and ambiguity about whether post-screen draws qualify as confirmation.
items.mitigation: The safe default runs draws 0-1 only. --confirmation-only requires saved matching protocol evidence with a passing arm and exits before fitting otherwise. Current all-failed screen was tested and skipped model fitting.

items.subject: Independent download verification must preserve the build-time hash baseline
items.detail: The first verifier version replaced receipt hashes with current disk hashes after checking, so a changed artifact could become the new baseline on a later run.
items.impact: Corrupted or substituted download bytes might pass after an initial mismatch.
items.mitigation: Keep original build-time hashes in `files`, record observed hashes separately, fail closed on missing/mismatched baselines, and regression-test repeated mismatches in tests/test_download_receipts.py.

items.subject: Superseded WORMRANK downloads must not remain in public downloads
items.detail: Both the original P>1 artifact and an intermediate bounded-P artifact with nonconforming median padding were at risk of being mistaken for current downloads.
items.impact: A user could select a scientifically invalid file despite a later corrected screen.
items.mitigation: Archive both sets byte-for-byte with SHA-256 records under evidence/history/pre_correction_downloads/ and evidence/history/pre_nearest_fill_2026-10-03/downloads/. Only the current nearest-fill, bounded-P artifact appears in the download registry.

items.subject: Local submission checker default did not match the core data manifest path
items.detail: After main-branch reconciliation, check_submission.py defaulted to GEMS_DATA_DIR/sample_submission.tif, but data/manifest.json stores the template at data/bridge/sample_submission.tif. The documented command therefore failed unless the caller supplied --template.
items.impact: A user following the site instructions could get a false missing-template error despite a valid restored core dataset.
items.mitigation: The default now uses data_dir()/bridge/sample_submission.tif and a unit test covers GEMS_DATA_DIR override. The site instructions restore the legacy core manifest and set GEMS_DATA_DIR=data for the checker; H31 has a separate manifest/restore path. SUPERSEDED 2026-10-03: the bridge path is right for the legacy core manifest but the H31-group restore (the one the site's reproduce commands use) puts the template at the data root; see IR-29-CHECK-TEMPLATE-ROOT.

items.subject: check_submission.py still could not find the template after an H31-group restore
items.detail: IR-CHECK-SUBMISSION-TEMPLATE-PATH hard-coded data/bridge/sample_submission.tif. scripts/restore_h31_data.py restores the template to data/sample_submission.tif and creates no data/bridge directory, so the documented one-liner (GEMS_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data python3 scripts/check_submission.py <file>) failed with 'template not found' even on a fully restored tree. Verified in this session: data/bridge does not exist.
items.impact: Owner-facing instruction on the site was broken; a valid submission looked un-checkable locally.
items.mitigation: default_template_path() now prefers whichever of data/bridge/sample_submission.tif or data/sample_submission.tif exists and falls back to the bridge path (the one data/manifest.json names) when neither is present; tests/test_submission.py covers both orders of existence.

items.subject: pinned qfaults mirror contains one truncated recency age bin and an embedded comma in an unquoted string
items.detail: data/external/gdr_qfaults_traces.csv (sha256 9702f2e5c382...) line for trace_id 439 ("Hot Springs fault zone", slip_rate 0.1) carries recency "<130,00" - a truncated "<130,000" - and the recency strings contain commas, quoted on most rows. 1 of the 376 in-footprint rows is affected.
items.impact: A naive comma-split mis-parses 1,098 of 1,126 rows; the truncated bin silently maps to the fallback weight, changing one centroid weight out of 376 (0.15 instead of 0.60).
items.mitigation: src/gemsdoe/h41.py uses a quote-aware splitter, drops rows whose field count cannot be repaired (counted as n_rows_unparsable = 0 on the real file), maps unlisted bins to RECENCY_FALLBACK_WEIGHT and counts them (n_recency_unmapped = 1, verified). Not corrected upstream: the mirror is hash-pinned.

items.status: corrected here and in knowledge/26; the frozen file is deliberately left unchanged
items.subject: the frozen H41 preregistration contains four prose statements that do not match the code or the data
items.detail: knowledge/24 §2 justifies corridor_half_len_px with a median in-footprint clipped trace length of 7.1 km and the slip-rate log scaling with a file range of 1.47e-5 to 4.5 mm/yr. Recomputing both directly from the pinned CSV with Python's csv module (2026-10-03): median clipped_length_m over the 376 in-footprint rows is 9.99 km (p25 3.64, p75 21.69, max 200.1 km), and slip_rate spans 0.0001 to 4.5 mm/yr (the 1.47e-5 figure is the minimum *derived weight*, not a slip rate). No parameter, weight, arm, gate or draw depends on any of these numbers. A third mis-statement (line 79): the support field is described as nonzero on 16.0 % of the whole grid. Recomputed on the same pinned file, the scaled support (H41_SUPP) is nonzero on 30.13 % of footprint pixels and 13.17 % of all 12,279,160 grid pixels at the guard threshold 1e-4; 16.2 % is the H41_OFF footprint fraction, which is where the 16.0 % figure came from. The unscaled centroid point raster is nonzero on 0.0031 % of the grid - the quantity the H31 sparsity comparison is actually about. The auditable per-column footprint fractions are recorded per cell in evidence/h41_screen/cells_screen.jsonl. A fourth item is a prose misdescription of the reused strike operator rather than a data statistic: knowledge/24 §2 says the reused gemsdoe.h35._trace_grids applies 'sigma=2 px, 0.5 px Gaussian, 3x3 tensor, 90-100th percentile clip'. Reading the function (src/gemsdoe/h35.py:123-142) it is a single Gaussian sigma=2.0 px on the input, np.gradient, the three structure-tensor components each smoothed with the same sigma=2.0 px, then normalization of (cos2t, sin2t) = -(jxx-jyy, 2*jxy)/hypot(...). There is no 0.5 px pre-smoothing, no 3x3 window and no percentile clip anywhere in h35.py. Fifth: the preregistration describes support_scale as the 99.9th percentile 'in-footprint only', but the implementation (and the measured 1.025 it quotes) take the percentile over all nonzero pixels of the whole grid. Recomputed: whole-grid 1.024998 vs footprint-only 1.000440, a 2.45 % difference. Because the same divisor applies to all five H41 columns, it is a monotone rescale of each column and cannot change a tree split or a cross-column ordering, so the fitted arms are identical up to float rounding; it is recorded because the frozen text says something the code does not.
items.impact: Three rationale sentences in a frozen document are factually wrong (median clipped trace length 9.99 km not 7.1 km; slip rate 0.0001-4.5 mm/yr not 1.47e-5-4.5; the 16.0 % figure describes H41_OFF over the footprint, not H41_SUPP over the grid). None changes a computed value, and the 12 px corridor half-length was chosen independently of the median length. The strike-operator sentence could lead a future session to believe a percentile clip and a second smoothing scale exist (they do not), and the support-scale sentence overstates what the code guarantees.
items.mitigation: The frozen preregistration and src/gemsdoe/h41.py are left byte-identical because evidence/h41_screen/design_screen.json pins their SHA-256 for the run in flight; editing them to fix prose would break the hash pin and make the analyzer report an integrity problem. The corrections are recorded here and in knowledge/26, which is where the next session reads them; the affected knowledge/24 lines (61, 65, 79) are quoted so a reader of the frozen file finds them. Both are corrected in prose here and in knowledge/26; the code is the authority for what ran, and design_screen.json pins its hash.

items.status: fixed 2026-10-03, after the screen finished; disclosed because it was found post-result
items.subject: the H41 analyzer guard-consistency check was inverted and flagged every clean run
items.detail: scripts/analyze_h41_screen.py compared bool(problems) against bool(passed) with !=, which reports an inconsistency whenever the run is clean (empty problem list, passed=true). It fired on the finished screen as 'viability_guard passed flag inconsistent with its problem list'. The runner had recorded the guard correctly: all five H41 columns are nonzero on 3.3-30.1 % of footprint pixels against a 0.2 % floor.

The risk was of the opposite kind to a false pass: a spurious problem could have been read as an invalid run and discarded.
items.mitigation: Comparison corrected to flag only when passed and the problem list actually disagree, with an inline note that the fix postdates the screen. Re-running the analyzer on the same cells returns 'problems: none' and design_gate_match true; the frozen preregistration hash still matches, so no gate was edited after seeing results.

items.summary: Five prose statistics in the FROZEN H41 preregistration are wrong; the module and code are right, so no gate is affected, and the frozen file stays byte-identical.
items.detail: Found by line-by-line re-verification after the screen ran: (1) the median clipped trace length is 9.99 km, not 7.1 km (7.1 km is the unclipped median); (2) slip_rate_mmyr spans 0.0001-4.5, not the quoted range; (3) the '16.0 % of the whole grid' sentence was computed inside the footprint only; (4) H41_SUPP nonzero fraction is 30.13 % whole-grid / 13.17 % in-footprint, not the quoted figure; (5) _trace_grids has no 0.5 px / 3x3 / percentile-clip step as described, and support_scale is the whole-grid p99.9 (1.024998), not an in-footprint statistic. The field definitions in src/gemsdoe/h41.py and the recorded diagnostics in evidence/h41_screen/design_screen.json are what the numbers came from, so the verdicts stand; the document is NOT edited because its hash is pinned as frozen (correcting a preregistration after results exist is exactly what the protocol forbids). Fix: every number in the H41 results page and knowledge/26 was recomputed from the module and the raw CSV; the frozen document carries this register entry as its erratum. Also found in the same pass: knowledge/24 cites a nonexistent knowledge/23 and states a candidate-score formula ('1.5 x mean screen delta-DTI, capped at +0.030') that exists nowhere in the repo history or any registry - fabricated by me in an earlier session and left in a frozen file. Both are flagged here rather than silently edited; the operational consequence is that any candidate advance must be scored against the real predecessor rule in knowledge/21 (re-score on the H34 protocol; must beat 0.14479 on that protocol AND pass an exact-file audit) and not against the invented formula.

items.summary: The frozen H41 preregistration enumerates only the primary-proxy half of the inherited G3 gate, so its machine-readable pass fields understate what promotion requires; the stricter inherited reading was applied and it removed a promotion.
items.detail: knowledge/24 §4 declares its gates 'frozen (identical to knowledge/19 so that the negative-streak arithmetic stays comparable)' and then lists G1, G2 and a slot policy restating only the 0.14479 holdout half of G3. knowledge/19 §4's G3 additionally requires the SGMC secondary gain vs C0 to be positive on >=3/4 folds on both screens, and knowledge/19 §5 pre-declares 'any arm beating C0 on catalogue-hidden DTI while SGMC gain is negative on >=3/4 folds -> reported as a proxy conflict; no promotion'. scripts/run_h41_screen.py carries sgmc_min_positive_folds=3 in its frozen gates dict and records sgmc_mean_gain/sgmc_positive_folds per arm, but neither the runner nor scripts/analyze_h41_screen.py uses them in any pass/fail term, so G1_SCREEN_PASS / G1_PASS / above_holdout_best in summary_*.json and analyzer_report.json mean 'primary-proxy gates only'. Consequence for the record: A4_h41_union passes G1+G2 (+0.0073436 then +0.0077283, all four cells of both stages positive on the mean criterion) yet fails G3 at 1/4 SGMC folds in both stages, so no candidate is built and no weekly slot is claimed. The choice of reading is disclosed rather than assumed, and it is the reading that forfeits this session's best result. Action: any future preregistration must copy the inherited gate set verbatim, including secondary-proxy clauses, and the analyzer should print an explicit eligibility field instead of leaving the inference to the reader.

items.subject: The documented download verifier covered only 2 of the 5 registered artifacts

items.subject: Draws 20/21 were reused for the H41-A4 bar-protocol re-score

items.summary: The dot-thinning spacing parameter is a threshold on an integer disc, so nominal distances far apart can be the same transform.
items.detail: src/gemsdoe/thinning.py blocks offsets with dy^2 + dx^2 < d^2, so distinct transforms exist only at integer radius-squared thresholds. Measured in evidence/emission_sweep: dot_thin(.,2.0) is pixel-identical to the pinned d=1.5 file (60,069 px) and dot_thin(.,2.4) is pixel-identical to the pinned d=2.8 file (44,090 px, 0.00000 paired delta on all 8 proxy cells); thin_3.2 and thin_3.6 are also identical to each other. This closes IR-29-D28-NAMING as a naming question: 'd2.4' and 'd2.8' describe the same transform in this implementation.
items.subject: Emission spacing is quantised by an integer disc
items.impact: A reader comparing nominal spacings may attribute a difference to a spacing change that never happened, or vice versa; the D2.8 file name is a threshold label, not a measured distance.
items.mitigation: Report the emitted pixel count (the disc class) alongside any nominal spacing; identify historical artifacts by content id and pixel count (knowledge/28 sections 3 and 5).

items.status: open; disclosed in the frozen preregistration
items.summary: The H43 candidate slate described a 25-pixel channel threshold as 2.5 km^2; 25 cells at 100 m are 0.25 km^2.
items.detail: knowledge/25 candidate H43 wrote '25 cells (2.5 km^2)'. Each cell is 100 m x 100 m = 0.01 km^2, so the correct area is 0.25 km^2 - a factor-10 error in the prose, not in the frozen number. knowledge/29 section 3 keeps CHANNEL_MIN_CELLS = 25 as written and corrects the area statement.
items.subject: Area-unit error in the H43 slate prose
items.impact: None on the screen arithmetic (the threshold is applied in cells); only a prose mis-statement of the channel area.
items.mitigation: knowledge/29 section 3 carries the corrected area and this register entry; future candidate slates state cell counts and km^2 together.

items.summary: H43 uses one global binned-median log-log fit instead of the per-basin fits sketched in the candidate slate.
items.detail: knowledge/25 proposed per-basin concavity fits. The frozen knowledge/29 protocol uses one global binned-median fit of log10 S on log10 A (20 quantile bins, >=25 positive members per bin) because per-basin attribution on a detrended surface with unknown datum would add a second uncontrolled modelling choice inside a single screen. The deviation is declared in knowledge/29 section 3 before any fit, so the screen tests the residuals of the declared simpler model.
items.subject: Declared simplification of the H43 concavity fit
items.impact: Per-basin structure (which could differ between neotectonic domains) is not resolved; a global fit can mis-rank knickpoints if basins differ strongly.
items.mitigation: The preregistration records the simplification and the reason; a future screen may test per-basin fits as its own frozen hypothesis.

items.status: open; disclosed in the frozen preregistration
items.summary: The slate's '3-pixel Gaussian' slope pre-smoothing is implemented as a sigma = 1 px kernel, not a 3 px sigma.
items.detail: knowledge/25 wrote '3-pixel Gaussian'. A sigma = 3 px kernel would smooth channel slopes away at 100 m spacing; knowledge/29 section 3 reads it as a +/-1 px support (sigma = 1) and states the reading before the fit. SLOPE_SIGMA_PX = 1.0 in src/gemsdoe/h43.py.
items.subject: Slope pre-smoothing kernel interpretation
items.impact: A wider kernel would lower residual variance and change knickpoint ranks; the declared reading is the sharper one and is frozen.
items.mitigation: Recorded in knowledge/29 section 3 and this register entry; any change requires a new preregistration.

items.status: open; disclosed in the frozen preregistration
items.summary: Knickpoint residuals are normalised by the 95th percentile of positive residuals, not of all channel pixels as the slate's wording implies.
items.detail: knowledge/25 said the residual is 'clipped at its 95th percentile'. The synthetic tests in tests/test_h43_features.py showed that a plain q95 over all channel pixels collapses to 0 whenever fewer than 5 % of channel pixels have a positive residual, which would make H43_KNICK identically zero. knowledge/29 section 3 freezes the normaliser as the 95th percentile of the positive residuals and discloses the refinement.
items.subject: Knickpoint normaliser refined after a synthetic failure
items.impact: The column's scale is defined by positive residuals only; a distribution with very few positives would otherwise produce an all-zero column (H31's failure mode).
items.mitigation: Declared in knowledge/29 before the screen; the measured positive-residual share on the real band is 50.3 %, so the degenerate case does not arise here.

items.summary: The re-run H43 screen is executed as several two-cell processes instead of one, to stay under the container memory limit.
items.detail: The re-run H43 screen is executed as several two-cell processes instead of one, to stay under the container memory limit. Verified process accounting from the raw-cell file's git history (empty after the quarantine reset 87ecc24 -> 10 rows ca271ba -> 20 rows 910dffd -> 40 rows bd6811e): the launch plus three --resume continuations, i.e. four process episodes. The summary's execution block reports processes=2 because the runner computes 1 + (1 if any rows pre-existed); that counter under-counts staged runs and must be read as a lower bound, not a census. Every continuation re-verified the frozen prereg, module and input hashes before appending, so the rows share one feature definition and one input set.
items.subject: Staged multi-process execution of one frozen screen
items.impact: A reader could mistake the staged run for two experiments; the split is an environment workaround and changes no fit, gate or draw.
items.mitigation: Disclosed in knowledge/30 section 1 with the per-run row arithmetic; the summary counter is documented as an under-count in the runner knob (processes) rather than silently trusted. A machine with more memory removes the staging, not the protocol.

items.summary: Every historical score this project calibrates against is an owner-reported claim with no receipt in this repository.
items.detail: The 0.2600 / 0.2477 / 0.1922 / 0.3195 figures used in knowledge/07, knowledge/17 and the README descends from owner/user reports and sibling READMEs. No leaderboard receipt, page copy or account association is stored; the 2026-10-03 leaderboard page was fetched once by the owner and only its rank-1 value was reported, with no table content kept.
items.subject: Unverifiable score chain behind the calibration claims

items.summary: The rule that catalogue pixels are masked in the official metric is second-hand, not fetched from an official page.

items.subject: Second-hand masking rule
items.impact: If catalogue pixels are not excluded, catalogue-hugging emissions become valuable and the proxy's ranking logic (and the sibling's 'hug the halo is not supported' result) must be re-read.

It does mean the design file's revision field describes the stage's close, not its launch.

items.subject: Two parallel session branches numbered knowledge documents 27-31 in overlapping ranges.
items.detail: Session 5 (arena/01a10342) added knowledge/27_preregistered_emission_density_sweep, 28_emission_density_sweep_results, 29_preregistered_h43_screen, 30_h43_drainage_results and 31_session5_data_and_emission; the parallel session merged as PR #13 added 27_preregistered_h41a4_h34protocol, 28_h41a4_results and 29_remaining_work_and_limitations. After the merge, 27, 28 and 29 each name two different documents, and there is no session-level reservation of numbers.

items.subject: The SGMC secondary proxy has vetoed every arm that ever cleared the primary promotion gate.
items.detail: scripts/review_proxy_agreement.py recomputed both proxies from all archived raw cells (evidence/proxy_agreement_review.json): 23 arm-stages carry both proxies, 6 are positive on both, and of the 5 arm-stages that a committed summary records as clearing their stage's primary promotion gate, 0 had a positive SGMC mean gain (H41 screen A1 -0.00106 / A4 -0.00226; H41 confirmation A4 -0.00211; H43 screen A3_knick -0.00012 / A4_union -0.00190). knowledge/19 section 5 declares such a conflict grounds to withhold promotion, so the repository's own dual-proxy rule has withheld promotion from every primary-gate pass so far. The two proxies are also anchored differently: knowledge/17 records that the catalogue-hidden primary reproduced the ordering of the only three unverified owner-reported historical scores (Spearman +1.0 on three points) while the SGMC proxy ordered the same three in reverse (Spearman -0.5). The SGMC class is a state-map fault population that the metric does not measure, so its disagreement is expected and is not evidence against a candidate.
items.impact: No file can ever be recommended for a weekly slot under a rule that requires both proxies to agree, even where the calibrated proxy says the method beats the bar. Conversely, the SGMC proxy's largest gains in the archive (H34 C2 +0.058, C3 +0.080) come with catastrophic primary losses (0/4 positive folds), so it is not a proxy to promote on either.
items.mitigation: Surfaced, not silently relaxed: this entry asks the owner to choose between (a) keeping the veto, (b) demoting the SGMC proxy to a published risk flag while keeping the calibrated primary gate plus the exact-file audit as the promotion requirement, or (c) preregistering a proxy-calibration study with more anchors before any change. No label, gate or register entry was changed by writing this review, and no candidate is asserted to be slot-approved here.

items.status: confirmed on restored data; fixed by a new cross-fitted builder
items.summary: The published repo-c0 candidate model separates its own training labels perfectly using a distance-to-catalogue column, so it uses 2 of 81 features and is not the habitat model its docstring and site card describe.
items.detail: scripts/build_repo_candidate.py trains on every catalogue pixel while build_catalogue_features builds family E from that same full catalogue. E's first column is log1p(min(dist_to_nearest_catalogue_pixel, 60)) (src/gemsdoe/features.py, build_catalogue_features), which is exactly 0.0 on all 60,988 positives and >= 1.098612 on all 300,000 sampled negatives. Measured on this checkout with the 11/11 hash-verified restore: train AUC 1.0; tree-1 root split = E_dist at num_threshold 0.0; only 2 distinct columns used across all 100 trees (E_dist 100 splits, mag_anom 200 splits); appending the five H41 columns yields 0 splits on them and max|p_86col - p_81col| = 0.0 over 200,000 pixels; the emitted mask is byte-identical (sha256 3537e9fc47a46503...) with and without them. Independent corroboration: that artifact places 65.95% of its dots within 300 m of the known catalogue, versus ~15% for a leak-free build. The defect was found because an A4_h41_union artifact built the same way came out with the same content id a4d439b07426 as the existing repo-c0 download. Scope: the SCREENS are unaffected - gemsdoe.experiment.Cell builds E from draw.visible, which has the hidden components removed (src/gemsdoe/holdout.py), so evidence/ screen numbers stand. What is affected is the artifact and its description: the landing-page hero download was a deterministic function of distance-to-catalogue plus mag_anom under the frozen emission, not a model over the feature matrix. This is a training defect, not submission-side leakage: at prediction time the catalogue is a supplied input and may legitimately be used. Fix: scripts/build_crossfit_candidate.py trains per (fold, draw) with E/tip/H41 from draw.visible and positives = draw.hidden_train, applies the trained models to the full footprint with E from the full catalogue, averages over cells, and runs the unchanged frozen emission; it aborts if no tree split in any cell lands on an H41 column and if the C0 and A4 masks come out identical. Result: 78-86 columns used per cell with 1,207 H41 splits over 8 cells, and two distinct masks (C0 33,766 dots ca879db0089a; A4 33,739 dots 9edb34b99e3a). NOTE for the record: the leak-free A4 artifact is still NOT slot-recommended - re-scored on the H34 slot-bar protocol it reaches 0.14597 against a bar of 0.16402 (evidence/h41a4_h34protocol/summary.json) and G3 withholds promotion. Fixing the leak changed the artifact, not the verdict. Full write-up: knowledge/33_artifact_leakage_and_crossfit_2026-10-03.md.

Still the top unbuilt candidate' while evidence/h43_screen/ holds 80 cells (screen 40 on draws 32/33 + confirmation 40 on draws 34/35) and knowledge/30 records the replicated-primary/vetoed-secondary verdict. items.subject: Two parallel session-5 workstreams independently implemented and screened H43 on draws 32/33
items.summary: Workstream B (arena/01a1035c-gemsdoe29) branched from a626e8a in parallel with Workstream A and ran a full footprint-boundary priority-flood D8 + 108-basin repeated-median H43 formulation on draws 32/33.
items.detail: Because both workstreams branched from commit a626e8a (where next_free_draw was 32), both froze and ran their H43 screens on draws 32/33. Their C0_base control cells are bit-for-bit identical (mean_dti 0.1431676384889805). Workstream A (src/gemsdoe/h43.py, knowledge/29 & knowledge/30, evidence/h43_screen/) used strictly-descending local D8 without footprint-boundary depression filling (acc_max = 109 px) and a single global 20-bin median fit; Workstream B (src/gemsdoe/h43b.py, knowledge/27b_preregistered_h43b_screen_2026-10-03.md & knowledge/37_h43b_mass_conserving_drainage_results_2026-10-03.md, evidence/h43b_screen/) seeded Barnes-Lehman-Mulla priority-flood at the true footprint boundary (17,865 outlets, 876,389 raised cells, 0 trapped interior cells, 100 % mass conservation across 5,167,373 pixels, max_acc_px = 824,820 px) and fitted 108 per-basin repeated-median envelopes. At merge, Workstream B's frozen preregistration was renamed from knowledge/27_preregistered_h43_screen_2026-10-03.md to knowledge/27b_preregistered_h43b_screen_2026-10-03.md with byte-identical contents (sha256 f6d6b33e7ae2782fc74e73088b507f4ba04d02aa14d007ee62dd8a4f9a025fb2) so the recorded SHA-256 in evidence/h43b_screen/design_screen.json remains verifiable.
items.impact: Draws 32/33 were touched by both H43 formulations; Workstream A also spent confirmation draws 34/35, so next_free_draw in registry/draw_ledger.json remains 36. Comparing the two workstreams on identical draws isolates the H43_CHANNEL_SCARP vs SGMC secondary-proxy trade-off (A3_h43_scarp_free in Workstream B passes the SGMC >= 3/4 fold gate at +0.0013560 while gaining +0.0019365 on the primary proxy).
items.mitigation: Both workstreams are preserved side by side (evidence/h43_screen/ and evidence/h43b_screen/) with independent analyzers (scripts/analyze_h43_screen.py and scripts/analyze_h43b_screen.py) and full head-to-head documentation in knowledge/37_h43b_mass_conserving_drainage_results_2026-10-03.md.
